column1: # tools.tsv — every AI CLI tmux-ai-sessions-restore knows how to resume. The single source of
# truth for the save/restore path: tools.awk (plan.awk, rewrite.awk), helpers.sh and the TPM
# entrypoint all read it. Adding a CLI = one row here + its install_<tool>/uninstall_<tool>
# functions in install_hooks.sh / uninstall_hooks.sh (capture is inherently tool-specific).
# Tab-separated, one row per tool, every cell non-empty ("-" = none). Columns:
#   1 tool       name used in @ai_tool, @ai-restore-enabled-tools, @ai-restore-<tool>-command
#   2 regex      ERE for the CLI process: matched against the basename of comm, of argv[0],
#                and (for node/bun) of the first non-option argument (the script)
#   3 base       default launch command (override per tool with @ai-restore-<tool>-command)
#   4 resume     appended to the base to resume; {id} is replaced by the session id
#   5 id_flags   comma list of argv words followed by the session id on a running CLI's
#                command line: `--f v`, and `--f=v` for flags starting with `--`; a bare word
#                is a subcommand (`codex resume <id>`)
#   6 pin_flags  like id_flags, but lower priority: an id the CLI was pinned to at launch
#   7 id_fmt     uuid (exactly a UUID) | safe ([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*)
#   8 match      word resurrect matches in the saved command (`~<match>` in
#                @resurrect-processes); also how a recorded command is recognised as this tool's
#   9 oneshot    comma list marking a non-interactive run whose prompt hook must not take over
#                the pane: a flag (`-p`) anywhere, or a bare word = the subcommand (`run`)
